preamble: Depharyngealization of the voiced pharyngeal [ʕ] (Semitic ʿayin) to the glottal stop [ʔ] moves the constriction from the pharynx down to the glottis. It is a recurrent outcome in Semitic: Standard Israeli Hebrew merged ע with א as /ʔ/ (or zero), and Amharic lost its pharyngeals by the end of the medieval period, so that the ʿayin series of the Ge'ez script is now read [ʔ].

examples.to: Modern Israeli /ˈajin/, with ע realized as [ʔ] or zero
examples.note: In Standard Israeli Hebrew /ʕ/ for ע has been absorbed by /ʔ/, the sound traditionally used only for א; the distinction survives in the speech of older Sephardim and Mizrahim.
Pre-17th-century Amharic still distinguished /ʔ/ and /ʕ/; phonological change merged them, so the ʿayin (ዐ) and ʾalef (አ) series of the script both represent [ʔ].
